Oct. 20, the Boston Globe: “Many voters believe Massachusetts has become a worse place to live, a Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll found. They want to reelect Governor Maura Healey anyway.”

The numbers: 42% say worse. 15% say better. 55% say taxes are too high. Healey leads Republican Mike Minogue, 59% to 36%.

Massachusetts has a Democratic governor and Democratic supermajorities in both chambers: 35 of 40 Senate seats, 131 House seats.

One party owns the results. The Globe called it “a worse place.” FNN fixed one word: the worst.

stories.headline: Ed Markey Wants to Abolish the Fire Department While His State Hands Out Matches
stories.deck: Markey calls ICE “thugs” over street arrests. His own state’s rules are why ICE makes street arrests.
stories.body:
Sen. Ed Markey, Oct. 19: “Trump’s ICE thugs.” In September he called ICE “a domestic terror organization.”

Here’s why agents are on the street. In 2017, Massachusetts’ highest court ruled local officials can’t hold anyone solely on an ICE detainer. Boston’s Trust Act limits cooperation with federal immigration authorities. In January, Gov. Healey barred ICE from using state property as a staging area.

In May 2025, ICE said many of its 1,461 Massachusetts arrests came after local jurisdictions “refused to honor immigration detainer requests.”

Lock the jailhouse door. Then complain about the sidewalk.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Said It Never Debanks for Politics. Here’s What the Federal Regulator Found.
stories.deck: A bank’s CEO can say anything at a shareholder meeting. A watch list is harder to argue with.
stories.body:
May 21, 2019, JPMorgan’s shareholder meeting. Jamie Dimon: “We have not and do not debank people because of their political views.”

Oct. 14, 2026: the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency found that from 2020 to September 2025, all nine of the largest banks had such policies.

JPMorgan’s payment company flagged “MAGA, Make America Great, and America First.” An employee scrubbed “right wing” and “religious” from a nonprofit’s file.

To be fair: one bank turned away a group whose political arm endorsed only Democrats. The weight of the examples is not close.
